problem: If $\overset{―}{A}={l,m,n,o}$ and $\overset{―}{B}={k,l,o,p,q,r},$ then what is $\overset{―}{A\cup B}?$
worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for unions states that

$$
\overset{―}{A\cup B}≡\overset{―}{A}\cap \overset{―}{B}.
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A\cup B} & =\overset{―}{A}\cap \overset{―}{B} \\  & ={l,m,n,o}\cap {k,l,o,p,q,r} \\  & ={l,o}.\end{aligned}
$$
